content: Metabolife is an American company that specialized in the production of dietary supplements. Its most popular product, Metabolife 356, was an ephedra-based supplement that once achieved annual sales exceeding $1 billion. However, Metabolife 356, along with other supplements containing ephedra, was associated with thousands of severe adverse health events, including fatalities. These safety concerns led the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to ban all dietary supplements containing ephedra in 2004, deeming them unsafe for consumption. The founder of Metabolife, Michael Ellis, faced legal charges for providing false statements to the FDA. He was accused of attempting to obstruct regulatory oversight of ephedra-containing products. Additionally, Metabolife became the subject of investigations by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and the Department of Justice (DOJ) for income tax evasion. The company ultimately admitted to filing fraudulent tax returns and was ordered to pay a criminal fine of $600,000. William Bradley, the owner of Metabolife, also pled guilty to evading millions of dollars in taxes. As a result, he was sentenced to six months in federal prison and two years of probation. Following a significant decline in sales and facing over $1 billion in personal injury lawsuits related to Metabolife 356, the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in 2005. In late 2006, Metabolife's assets, including a substantial collection of artwork, were sold off to repay creditors and resolve outstanding personal injury claims.
